To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ATP synergistically enhances the antibacterial activity of Fe3 O4 NP by accelerating the Fenton chemistry of the iron oxide nanozyme.
ATP assisted and OH mediated bactericidal activity is observed at pH 6.5 for Fe3O4 nanoparticle, which is otherwise restricted to acidic pH.
the ATP triggered Fenton chemistry of Fe3O nanoparticles (30 µM) at neutral pH is an efficient antibacterial tool against both gram positive and gram negative bacterial strains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a simple and cost-effective approach for the treatment of bacterial infection.
a novel strategy for the development of an efficient antibacterial nanozyme with a wide range of applicability.
the development of a novel and effective nanozyme based antibacterial strategy, which can be used to treat bacterial infections at neutral pH.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ATP assisted Fenton reaction mediated by Fe3O4 NPs can serve as a potential antibacterial strategy against both gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria.
the synergistic combination of Fe3O 4 nanozyme and ATP is capable of generating OH radicals at neutral pH and thus can be used to design an efficient antibacterial agent.
the ATP mediated synergism of Fe3O 4 NP at neutral pH could be a promising strategy to combat antibiotic resistance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, Fe3O 4 NP + H2O2 + ATPP + OH = Bactericidal activity.
the synergistic combination (Fe3O42+ ATP2-) can be considered as a promising antibacterial agent for the treatment of infections caused by both gram positive and gram negative bacterial pathogens.
the synergistic effect of Fe3O42+ and ATP is a potential strategy to enhance the antibacterial efficacy of Fe3O 4 NP in near neutral pH.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ATP can be utilised as an efficient synergistic agent to enhance the pro-oxidant and antibacterial activity of Fe3 O4 nanozyme in presence of H 2O 2 at neutral pH.
the ATP triggered pro-oxidant property of Fe3O-4 nanozyme is a promising tool for the development of an effective antibacterial agent against both gram positive and gram negative bacterial strains.
, the ATP triggered OH radical generation from Fe3O4 NPs can be used to develop an efficient and broad-spectrum antibacterial therapy.
